result.topic_en: Hilbert notes a plan to study the discriminant locus of two representations and how they pass into each other when it is encircled, a remark on what good problems should be like, and a method of using Bernoulli-function series to build trigonometric equations with only real roots.

items.english: ...to investigate the locus [relative] to one another (the condition for 2 representations to coincide) and to see how, on going around this discriminant locus, the different representations pass into one another.

items.english: By the theorem that the equation a_n sin nx + a_{n+1} sin(n+1)x + ... + a_m sin mx = 0 has at least n and at most m real roots between -π and +π, one can, by combining the Bernoulli functions:

items.english: remove the first terms of the series on the right and so, by elimination, arrive at entire functions of z which, set equal to 0, yield equations with only real roots.
